narrative: Spend held roughly flat at ₹6,251 (from ₹6,162, up 1.5%), but Meta-reported purchases fell to 14 (from 22, down 36.4%), pushing cost per purchase (Meta) up sharply to ₹446 (from ₹280, up 59.4%). This reverses last read's reported rebound (16 purchases, ₹379 cost per purchase) — the most recent 1-2 days in this window are the freshest pulled data and most exposed to the attribution lag flagged previously, so some of this drop should self-correct in the next pull.

Shopify's own numbers moved in the same direction, though: orders fell to 16 (from 24, down 33.3%) and revenue fell to ₹28,488 (from ₹42,732, down 33.3%), pushing ROAS down to 4.56x (from 6.94x). Because Shopify counts confirmed orders rather than Meta's ad-attributed purchases, this side isn't subject to the same attribution lag — so while some of the Meta-side purchase drop is likely reporting lag, the matching Shopify decline suggests last read's one-window uptick (flagged explicitly as 'not confirmation the decline is over') did not hold, and order volume has genuinely stepped back down.

CTR extended its climb for a fourth straight read, up to 2.46% (from 2.17% this window, and above last read's reported 2.39%) — a genuinely positive trend running counter to the order/revenue softness. Hook rate held close to last read's reported level at 21.89% (from 26.57% this window, but essentially flat against last read's 21.56%), suggesting the earlier sharp hook rate decline has stabilized rather than continuing.

The anchor ad, 'VP_Umbartha_VideoAD_14-04-2026 – Copy', pulled back further to ₹4,403 (from ₹5,524, down 20.3%), a sharper step-down than last read's more modest pullback, while its own CTR improved to 2.34%. These three continue to look like durable, stable options even as the anchor keeps shrinking.
